author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman asked President Donald Trump for military assistance against Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthis, three sources familiar with the matter told Reuters. The sources said the leaders spoke at least twice Thursday and that the United States did not agree to conduct strikes, instead offering help with intelligence sharing and targeting.

The White House did not confirm the calls. A senior administration official said the United States remained in continuous dialogue with Saudi Arabia and Yemen’s government, with a focus on freedom of navigation and support for regional partners. Saudi Arabia’s government media office did not immediately respond to Reuters’ request for comment. Two sources also said the head of U.S. Central Command traveled to Saudi Arabia for talks Thursday.

The reported request came as Houthi forces advanced along Yemen’s Red Sea coast and reached Perim Island in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, according to Yemeni government sources. Control near that shipping corridor could add pressure to energy and cargo routes already strained by reduced traffic through the Strait of Hormuz. The situation remains fluid.
dek: Three sources told Reuters that Washington declined direct strikes while offering intelligence sharing and targeting assistance as Red Sea tensions rose.
headline: Saudi crown prince sought U.S. military help against Houthis, sources say
